context: A chess queen can attack a piece at any distance along its row, column, or either diagonal. On this 4×4 board, rows are numbered from top to bottom and columns from left to right, both starting at 1.
description: The left board has a queen at row 2, column 2, or (2, 2). No other queen can occupy a square in that row, column, or either diagonal. These four lines rule out 11 other squares in all.
The right board shows a valid placement. The first table lists the squares ruled out by the queen on the left board. The second gives the chosen column in each row of the right board.

frames.explanation: A valid placement satisfies all four constraints at once: no shared row, column, upper-left to lower-right diagonal, or upper-right to lower-left diagonal. Placing one queen per row automatically prevents row conflicts, but the column and both diagonals still need checking.
frames.title: Queens cannot share a row, column, or diagonal

summary: The left board shows the 11 squares that a single queen rules out along its row, column, and two diagonals. The right board shows a four-queens solution that satisfies every constraint.
